even with encrypt=false, mssql-jdbc negotiates login-time TLS the plaintext proxy cannot satisfy; the login handshake fails. Needs proxy TLS termination (C3F57E74). Same expected for msodbcsql18 / Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.
CREATE #temp (pins) then client drops -> pinned-discard fires (sessions_pinned+1, pool_discards+1) and frees the token; a fresh client connects immediately (no slot leak)
6 concurrent pinned sessions vs pool-max=2 -> exactly 2 acquire a backend, 4 hit acquire-timeout backpressure; pool never opens >2 backends (semaphore ceiling holds, no token leak)
5 truncated PRELOGIN connects dropped before login -> 0 backend slots reserved/leaked (pool_cold_opens unchanged); proxy remains usable
client hard-closes the socket mid-result-set (capturing dialer) -> proxy discards the mid-stream backend (pool_discards+1), does NOT return it; fresh client gets a clean backend (no half-read reuse)
backend restarted while client holds BEGIN TRAN -> in-txn statement fails cleanly (Read: EOF, no hang), backend discarded (pool_discards+1), fresh client connects+queries after recovery (no leak)
encrypt=on (legacy TDS 7.x, TLS handshake tunneled in PRELOGIN packets) terminated by the proxy; backend connection stays plaintext; SELECT 1 ok. Was 'unhandled' before #6.
encrypt=strict (TDS 8.0, TLS-first) terminated by the proxy; client must trust the proxy cert (strict ignores TrustServerCertificate by design); SELECT 1 ok. Was 'unhandled' before #6.
via TLS termination (#6); SELECT 1 — no session state. Also verified at encryption=strict.

ODBC Driver 18 issues [sys].sp_datatype_info_100 on EVERY connect. Was fail-safe PINNED as an unrecognized RPC → false-pinned every ODBC connection, killing pooling (the case-(a) risk #3 predicted). FIXED: read-only catalog procs whitelisted (no session state).

REAL BUG surfaced by #3: .NET reusing a pyodbc/ODBC-opened pooled backend intermittently mis-parsed responses (invalid TDS type token). Root cause: the backend's response wire-format is fixed by the COLD opener's replayed LOGIN7 (packet size + FeatureExt: pyodbc≠.NET) and RESETCONNECTION doesn't renegotiate it; the pool key omitted the login profile. FIX: poolKey now folds tds.LoginProfile (TDS ver+packet size+flags+LCID+FeatureExt). Same-driver pooling preserved; cross-driver 8-errors/5-runs → 0/6.

ORM (#3 'at least one ORM'). SQLAlchemy 2.0 runs the connection in manual-commit mode (autobegin), so EVERY unit of work — even a SELECT — opens an explicit transaction → TxMgr → pins. Correct (real open txn = session state), NOT a false-pin.
pins (temp table + the ORM's autobegin txn). Both encryption=on and strict verified.

CONSEQUENCE: a transactional ORM gets the proxy's connection CEILING but little warm-reuse (every session pins). AUTOCOMMIT isolation would let read-only ORM work multiplex; per-transaction multiplexing (#7) is what would recover pooling for transactional ORM workloads.
